content.comment_body: Hello, I sent a technician to a site with a [product_name] [version_no]. I had a [product_name] [version_no] at my desk and used the memory card with the updated program. However, at the site, although the new program appeared to be downloaded successfully, the old program remained on the device. The technician tried several times and each attempt seemed successful, but the old software persisted. We brought the memory card back to the office and tested it with the [version_no] version, and it worked. How can I prepare a memory card for an older [product_name] version without having the actual device available? I attempted to download the program to the [version_no] with the project set to [version_no] in the [product_name] engineering software. /[user_name]

You cannot use a program created with the device selection set to [product_name] [version_no] and saved on a memory card in a [product_name] [version_no]. The reverse, however, is possible. To resolve this, load the program from the memory card into the engineering software, change the device selection from [product_name] [version_no] to the older hardware type, and save it back to the card.

I transferred the software from the engineering tool to the [product_name] [version_no], setting it as [version_no] but it did not work as expected: engineering software [version_no] -> [product_name] [version_no] -> memory card memory card -> engineering software [version_no] -> Not working
Did you save the diagram as a binary dump file (".bin") on the memory card?
No, I prepared the memory card for the [product_name] [version_no]. Are you suggesting it's possible to create a memory card for a [product_name] without the actual device?

I did not say that. If you want the device to read the diagram from the memory card, you must store it in a specific format on the card, with the extension ".bin" instead of ".lsc". If you save a diagram for the older hardware type as a ".bin" file, then a newer device can read it. But if you store a diagram for the newer version as ".bin", the older version cannot read it.

Based on your explanation, that is exactly what you mean, which is good news for me. Previously, I thought you could only create a memory card for a device by uploading from the actual hardware or downloading to it with the card inserted. So to create a card for an older [product_name] (or other versions), I need to save the file as [product_name]_U_P.bin on a card using a PC?
Yes, as long as you set the correct device type in the engineering software before saving—selecting the appropriate model and version.
Thank you, I was not aware you could prepare a memory card for [product_name] in this way!

Hello, Here is the process: Open your program in the engineering software latest version. Press the relevant key (e.g. F2) and check the status window to see if the program is compatible with an older hardware type. If confirmed, switch the device configuration to the older hardware, use 'Save as,' and configure the appropriate settings as shown in the documentation.

analysis.insight_summary: Users struggled when transferring a program made on newer hardware to older hardware using a memory card. The older device would not accept the new program, despite following standard steps. Discussion clarified the confusion regarding cross-version compatibility and required file formats, such as .bin vs. .lsc. Users learned that specific hardware selection and proper file extension usage are crucial, which were initially non-obvious and led to programming issues.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to prepare or transfer a program from the latest hardware and deploy it via a memory card to older devices, all without needing physical access to the older hardware or facing compatibility problems.
